articles.title: Ozempic, Wegovy to carry new FDA warning over rare risk of vision loss
articles.summary:
Popular weight loss drugs including Ozempic and Wegovy will carry a new warning about a possible rare side effect that can sometimes lead to permanent vision loss, US health regulators announced Monday.
The Food and Drug Administration said the risk will be added to the labeling of all GLP-1 drugs, the blockbuster medications used to treat obesity, diabetes and several other medical conditions. The class includes a dozen injectable or pill-based drugs, including widely used brands like Zepbound and Mounjaro.
The eye condition, known as non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, can cause significant vision loss. The problem, which has been reported with all GLP-1 drugs, is caused by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve, although the underlying cause isn't understood, the FDA said.

articles.title: US stocks: Dow rockets 1,100 points, S&P over 2% as oil slide cools inflation worries; Nvidia slumps
articles.summary: US stocks rallied sharply on Monday as falling oil prices eased inflation concerns and helped the S&P 500 rebound from its steepest weekly decline since April 2025. Technology shares also surged, even as AI heavyweight Nvidia tumbled amid uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang, Reuters reported.The S&P 500 climbed 172.97 points, or 2.34%, to close at 7,549.83. The Nasdaq Composite gained 671.13 points, or 2.73%, to 25,250.55, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,104.20 points, or 2.16%, to 52,394.36.Stocks fell sharply last week after Democrats swept the US midterm elections, fuelling concerns that tighter regulations could threaten the durability of the artificial intelligence trade.Nine of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors gained more than 1% on Monday. Industrials and consumer discretionary led the advance, rising about 4% each.The broader market rallied despite a steep decline in Nvidia, the world’s second-most valuable company. Its shares touched their lowest intraday level since March 31 as investors questioned Huang’s future at the chipmaker following an internal investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.“The AI story is not going away if people are worried about that. The Democrats are not going to destroy AI. They can’t. It’s got a life of its own. They can put regulation around it, but they’re certainly not stopping it,” Ken Polcari, partner and chief market strategist at SlateStone Wealth in Jupiter, Florida told Reuters.A sharp decline in crude-oil prices provided further support by easing concerns about inflation after US President Donald Trump played down the likelihood of renewed strikes on Iran.“Oil prices for sure, if they’re down, that’s certainly adding fuel to the fire,” Polcari said.Investors are now awaiting key inflation reports. The Labor Department is scheduled to release October’s Consumer Price Index on Tuesday, followed by the Producer Price Index on Friday.Some Wall Street analysts described last week’s sell-off as an overreaction. Morgan Stanley and UBS said the rout in AI-linked stocks appeared excessive, arguing that the risk of severe restrictions on data-centre development remained low despite Democratic majorities in Congress.Expectations for an interest-rate increase at the Federal Reserve’s December meeting remained above 80%, according to CME FedWatch. October’s strong jobs report was seen as giving the central bank room to continue raising rates, even as oil prices eased.Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said on Monday that the central bank should adjust monetary policy “with care” as it formulates its response to inflation.Chipmakers rallied strongly. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped about 7% after tumbling more than 12% last week, its steepest weekly decline since the week ended April 4, 2025.Nvidia was the index’s only decliner on Monday, while Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices provided the biggest boosts.KKR shares advanced after the investment firm reported record quarterly profit. Constellation Energy, which has exposure to the AI infrastructure buildout, surged more than 10% after its adjusted third-quarter profit exceeded expectations.Berkshire Hathaway’s Class A shares also gained after the conglomerate reported lower third-quarter profit.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: Americans growing more worried about jobs amid rising prices, finds NY Fed survey

However, respondents also expressed greater confidence in their chances of finding employment after losing a job.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe growing pessimism over employment came alongside expectations that inflation would remain elevated. Consumers projected inflation at 3.9% over the next year, 3.3% over three years and 3% over five years, unchanged from September. All three readings remain above the Federal Reserve's 2% inflation target.Expectations for commodity prices were mixed, with households anticipating a more moderate rise in gasoline prices over the next year compared with their September projections.The survey's findings contrasted with official employment data released on Friday, which showed the US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, while the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%. The report also included significant upward revisions to recent hiring figures.Also Read: Fed’s Barkin urges rate policy caution, Goolsbee warns of inflation concerns as AI risks loomMeanwhile, households reported a modest improvement in their current financial situations, while expectations for their finances over the next year remained unchanged. Perceptions of access to credit, both currently and in the future, were also steady.The survey was conducted throughout October, ahead of the US midterm elections, which resulted in broad-based Democratic gains, including control of both houses of Congress.

articles.title: 5 reasons why Wall Street added $1.5T today
articles.summary: US stock market today, 9 November, 2026: Wall Street has added $1.5 trillion in market value, but the biggest surprise is where investors are putting their money. Semiconductor stocks are recovering, Tesla is climbing and oil prices are falling. The Dow Jones has gained more than 1,000 points, while the S&P 500 is up 2.17% and just 4% away from a record high. Yet Nvidia is falling nearly 5%.Monday's US stock market rally: Here's 5 reasons why Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq are rallying today1. AMD stock jumps 12% as investors return to semiconductor stocksAdvanced Micro Devices (AMD) is leading the semiconductor recovery. Its shares jumped more than 11% during Monday's trading and later extended gains to more than 12%, according to the latest November 9 update.The rally has two important drivers. First, investors are buying chip stocks after last week's heavy sell-off. Second, Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform and set a $600 price target.The company's growing AI business and its Google Cloud partnership are also supporting investor interest. AMD's rebound is particularly important because chipmakers were among the biggest losers during last week's technology sell-off.2. Tesla stock rises 5.45% as Magnificent Seven stocks recoverTesla (TSLA) shares climbed 5.45% to $377.74 in the November 9 market snapshot. The recovery reflects renewed buying across major technology companies after weeks of losses.Meta Platforms also gained around 5%, while Apple (AAPL) rose 2.16% to $349.77. Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft advanced more than 2%.These companies have significant weight in major US stock indexes. Their gains are helping the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recover. Tesla's rise also suggests investors are looking beyond semiconductor stocks for opportunities in the technology sector.3. Nvidia stock falls nearly 5% as Jensen Huang investigation unsettles investorsNvidia (NVDA) is moving in the opposite direction. Its shares fell 4.98% to $177.34 in the supplied midday snapshot, despite the broader technology rally.The pressure follows reports concerning CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Singapore-based business executive reportedly suspected of gathering information for China. Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship and said he would cooperate with the investigation.Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation. The company has said it has no reason to believe that national security or its business secrets were compromised.4. Broadcom and Marvell stocks jump more than 8% as AI chip demand returnsBroadcom (AVGO) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) each gained more than 8% on Monday. Intel (INTC) and Micron Technology (MU) also moved higher.The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) climbed more than 6%, showing that the recovery extends across the chip industry.Investors are returning to semiconductor companies after last week's selling raised questions about AI investment, data centre construction and future chip demand.However, the recovery does not mean those concerns have disappeared. Investors will continue watching technology companies' capital spending plans and demand for AI infrastructure.5. Constellation Energy and Barrick Mining stocks gain as earnings support Wall StreetConstellation Energy (CEG) shares climbed around 8%, while Barrick Mining (B) advanced approximately 4% following their quarterly results.Constellation is attracting attention because of its role in supplying electricity to data centres. Rising demand for computing power has made electricity availability an important part of the AI investment story.Barrick's gains also show that Monday's buying is not limited to technology companies. Investors are finding opportunities in other sectors as market sentiment improves.Why are oil prices falling while gold rises?Crude oil is another important part of Monday's market movement. WTI crude futures fell around 3.2% to $87.90 per barrel, while Brent declined approximately 4%.Investors are watching developments in the Iran war and the possibility that tensions could ease. Lower oil prices can reduce fuel costs for businesses and ease some inflation concerns.Gold moved in the opposite direction, rising 1.5% to around $4,140 an ounce. Bitcoin traded near $75,000 after retreating from weekend levels above $76,000. The 10-year US Treasury yield also moved higher to approximately 4.89% from Friday's 4.87%.Can the S&P 500 reach a new record high?Monday's rally comes after a difficult four weeks for Wall Street. The S&P 500 lost 5.6% over that period, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 10.2%. Both indexes recorded four consecutive weekly losses, their longest losing streaks since March.The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had reached record highs on October 6. articles.title: Nvidia CEO's secret affair has a hidden angle
articles.summary: The allegations on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang being targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation have brought a critical US national security concern into focus: whether access to one of America's most influential technology executives could have been used to gather sensitive information on its AI capabilities, semiconductor supply chains and strategy to maintain its lead over China.US intelligence agencies reportedly believe that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, was gathering information for Beijing after developing a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the US intelligence community believed she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.Also read: I was unfaithful to my wife: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits secret affair with Chinese spy Alice HuangWhile the allegations have not been independently established publicly, the potential national security implications are significant. Nvidia is a leading supplier of the advanced processors used to train and run AI models, and its technology has become central to America's efforts to maintain an advantage over China in artificial intelligence.The company's board has initiated an independent investigation, saying it has no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. However, the episode has prompted lawmakers to seek answers about the company's safeguards against foreign intelligence operations.Why is Nvidia so important to America's AI and military ambitions?Nvidia's importance extends beyond its position as one of the world's largest semiconductor companies. Its graphics processing units (GPUs) are used to train and operate advanced AI models, making them a critical part of the computing infrastructure underpinning the AI industry.The technology also has potential military and intelligence applications, including in autonomous systems, surveillance, cyber operations and other advanced defence capabilities.This is why access to advanced AI processors has become a strategic issue in the US-China rivalry. Washington has maintained restrictions on exports of its most advanced AI chips to China since 2022, citing concerns that the technology could accelerate Beijing's military modernisation.The stakes were highlighted in January, when former White House national security adviser Matt Pottinger told a congressional hearing that allowing Nvidia's H200 processors to be sold to China could strengthen Beijing's capabilities in areas ranging from nuclear weapons and cyber warfare to autonomous drones and intelligence operations, according to Reuters.The controversy involving Huang therefore raises a broader question: could access to the leadership of a company at the centre of America's AI infrastructure provide a foreign intelligence agency with information valuable to its technological and strategic ambitions?Also read: China dismisses 'Chinese spy' narrative in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang probe; calls it 'unsubstantiated'Could China have gained access to sensitive US technology or business information?One of the central concerns surrounding the reported intelligence operation is the possibility that proximity to Nvidia's CEO could have provided access to information about the company's technology, business strategy, customers and future product plans.The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Alice Huang's relationship with Jensen Huang could have provided her with insights into Trump's thinking on artificial intelligence.Nvidia has maintained that its cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information, not sensitive trade secrets or information related to US national security.Its board has also said it has no reason to believe that company secrets or national security were compromised.Also read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?Could the alleged operation have implications for US semiconductor export policy?Another important dimension is the potential access to information about Washington's semiconductor export restrictions and the discussions surrounding them.The US has sought to limit China's access to advanced AI processors, arguing that the technology could strengthen its military and intelligence capabilities.Nvidia, meanwhile, has a commercial interest in maintaining access to the Chinese market and has sought permission to sell certain advanced processors there.The Financial Times reported that US national security officials had privately expressed frustration with Huang over his efforts to persuade Trump to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to Chinese customers.The New York Times also reported that the relationship between Huang and Alice Huang could have provided her with insights into Trump's thinking on AI.This has raised questions about whether an intelligence operation targeting a senior technology executive could potentially provide information about US policy discussions, export restrictions and the positions of influential decision-makers.Megaspeed's involvement may raise supply chain concernsThe connection to Megaspeed adds another layer to the national security concerns.The Singapore-based data centre company buys equipment powered by Nvidia chips and rents computing capacity to businesses, including Chinese technology companies.According to The New York Times report, Megaspeed had bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years. The company has also come under US scrutiny over allegations that its network may have helped Chinese businesses access advanced AI processors restricted from export to China.The concern for Washington is that overseas data centres and intermediaries could potentially provide Chinese companies with access to computing resources powered by restricted American technology.The Financial Times also stated that a sister company in Malaysia bought at least $4.8 billion of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia technology between June 2024 and February 2026.In a Reuters column, Robyn Mak on Monday noted that Chinese technology companies have legally accessed processors restricted in mainland China through overseas data centres operated by neocloud providers such as Megaspeed. Mak also pointed to US investigations into suspected illegal chip-smuggling operations through Southeast Asia.The allegations therefore bring two national security concerns into focus: the possibility of foreign intelligence gathering around a major US technology company and the challenge of preventing restricted semiconductor technology from reaching Chinese customers through overseas supply chains.Could the controversy prompt tighter US export controls?The allegations could increase pressure on Washington to strengthen oversight of Nvidia's sales channels and the movement of advanced AI processors through third countries. US authorities have already been examining whether overseas companies and data centres are being used to circumvent restrictions on semiconductor exports to China.The controversy could intensify scrutiny of customer verification, the end-use of advanced chips and the role of intermediaries in the global AI computing supply chain.The issue is particularly sensitive as the Trump administration has been weighing how to balance US chipmakers' commercial interests against concerns about China's access to advanced AI technology.In December, Trump announced that the US would allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors to China under conditions that included a 25% fee for the US government. Regulations subsequently introduced requirements for third-party testing, customer security procedures and restrictions on the volume of chips that could be exported.The decision had already drawn criticism from China hawks in Washington, who argued that such sales could strengthen Beijing's military capabilities.Mak argued that the fallout could ultimately hurt China's AI ambitions more than it helps if Washington comes under pressure to tighten enforcement and close existing workarounds.Why are US lawmakers seeking answers from Huang?The national security implications have prompted congressional scrutiny.Three Republican committee chairmen — Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, John Moolenaar of the China Select Committee and Eric Crawford of the Intelligence Committee — have asked Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on November 18.In their November 4 letter, the lawmakers sought answers about his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.They said the allegations raised significant national security concerns about China's access to sensitive US technology and information.Separately, Democratic Senator Chris Coons has pledged to investigate the reported links between the Trump administration, Chinese intelligence and major AI industry executives, according to the Financial Times.The congressional inquiry could examine not just the reported relationship but also the extent to which Nvidia's customer interactions, information-sharing practices and security procedures protect sensitive American technology.What is at stake for the US-China AI race?The controversy comes as Washington and Beijing compete for leadership in artificial intelligence, an area often viewed as strategically important for economic competitiveness, military capabilities and technological influence.The US has sought to retain its advantage through restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports, while China has been working to develop domestic alternatives and secure access to computing resources.Nvidia occupies a particularly important position in this competition because its processors power a substantial part of the global AI infrastructure.Reuters columnist Mak noted that heightened scrutiny could accelerate the shift among Chinese companies towards domestic alternatives, including chips developed by Huawei and smaller competitors. However, the columnist also argued that tighter US restrictions could make it harder for Chinese technology companies to access advanced computing resources through overseas data centres.The controversy thus has implications beyond Nvidia. Any tightening of export controls or greater restrictions on overseas access to American AI processors could affect the pace at which Chinese companies develop and deploy advanced AI systems.Nvidia's board has initiated an independent investigation, overseen by independent directors and external legal counsel, where Huang has agreed to cooperate with the inquiry. The board has said it has no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's trade secrets were compromised.The US intelligence assessment concerning Alice Huang has not been publicly substantiated through disclosed evidence. China has rejected the espionage allegations as groundless speculation.The investigation and the congressional scrutiny will therefore be important in establishing whether any sensitive information was accessed, what information may have been sought and whether Nvidia's security protocols need to be strengthened.For Washington, the larger issue is how to protect the technology, expertise and supply chains underpinning its AI advantage at a time when competition with China is increasingly becoming a national security priority.

articles.title: All about Nvidia CEO Huang's affair controversy
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship with a business executive suspected by US intelligence of gathering information for Beijing, as the chipmaker's board launched an independent investigation into reports that its founder was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. While Huang has apologised to his family and company employees saying he was ‘unfaithful’ to his wife, Nvidia said it has no reason to believe that US national security or the company's secrets were compromised.US President Donald Trump has defended Huang, describing him as an "honourable guy" who has done an "amazing job" for the country. Trump also expects Huang to remain at the helm of Nvidia, adding that the executive deserved to have his side of the story heard.Also read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?The controversy follows reports by The New York Times and the Financial Times that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between the Nvidia leader and Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US intelligence officials reportedly believe she was gathering information for Beijing.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang issues key statementIn a draft email to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.”In a separate message reported by The New York Times, he apologised to his family and company employees, taking responsibility for his actions. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it," he wrote.Addressing Nvidia employees, Huang also acknowledged that he had fallen short of his responsibilities towards them. “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence," he said.He also requested privacy for his family, saying they bore no responsibility for his choices.Huang has not directly addressed the allegations that the business executive, aka, the Chinese spy was gathering information for the country. He has, however, supported Nvidia's investigation and committed to cooperate with it.Also read: Nvidia opens probe into CEO Jensen Huang over affair with woman suspected of spying for ChinaNvidia announces independent investigationNvidia's board of directors announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors, assisted by external independent legal counsel.In its statement, Nvidia said, "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." The company added that the board prioritised US national and economic security, which it said was paramount to Nvidia and its shareholders.The board also expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team and said it would provide further updates as appropriate.Huang, 63, will continue as Nvidia CEO during the investigation, it clarified.Speaking on Huang meeting thousands of customer executives every year, the company previously said that it regularly receives updates from the US government regarding parties and entities of concern and acts accordingly.Trump defends Nvidia CEOTrump has publicly defended Huang amid the controversy, describing him as an honourable person and praising his contribution to the US."I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on," Trump told reporters. "I think he's an honourable guy," he said, adding that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country".When asked whether Huang should remain Nvidia's CEO, Trump replied: "I think so. Sure."Trump also suggested that Huang should be given an opportunity to explain himself. Asked whether he would take Huang on his planned trip to Asia, Trump said, "I don't know, but I'd certainly take him."The remarks came amid reports that Trump had been briefed on intelligence findings concerning Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman roughly a year ago but had chosen not to act on the information, according to The New York Times.The Financial Times separately reported that a US government memo based on intelligence information about the alleged relationship had been shared with a small group of senior US officials shortly before Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.The FT also reported that Trump had held multiple meetings with Huang since beginning his second presidential term in 2025. Huang had personally lobbied Trump earlier this year to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to customers in China.Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese spy?Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese national and former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company.According to The New York Times, Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a senior executive at Megaspeed. The company buys equipment powered by Nvidia chips and rents computing capacity to businesses, including Chinese technology company Alibaba.US intelligence agencies reportedly concluded that Alice Huang had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang and was passing information directly to Beijing.The Financial Times reported that the US intelligence community believed she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main intelligence agency.Jensen Huang had previously described their association as a normal business relationship.Megaspeed and its connection to the Nvidia caseMegaspeed has come under US scrutiny over concerns that Nvidia's advanced AI chips may have been diverted to China.The New York Times reported that Megaspeed had been examined for potentially steering Nvidia AI chips to China. According to the publication, the firm bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years.The Financial Times reported that Megaspeed was spun off from a Chinese gaming company in 2023. US authorities have been investigating companies, particularly in Southeast Asia, suspected of helping China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export restrictions.Nvidia had previously launched an internal investigation into allegations concerning the diversion of chips through Megaspeed but assessed that there was no evidence of wrongdoing, according to the Financial Times.US lawmakers step up actionSenior Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives earlier asked Huang to brief Congress about the allegations and Nvidia's security protocols.In a letter dated November 4, Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, who leads the China Select Committee; and Eric Crawford, chairman of the Intelligence Committee, sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on November 18.The lawmakers sought answers about the New York Times report and Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage. The letter said the allegations raised significant national security concerns regarding China's access to sensitive US technology and information.The lawmakers added that Congress needed to determine the extent to which US national security had been placed at risk.Meanwhile, Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat who is due to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee from January, pledged to open an investigation."Congress will investigate and get answers," Coons wrote on X, referring to what he described as the relationship between the Trump administration, Chinese spies and AI billionaires.Political and corporate reactions to Jensen Huang affairUS Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment on the allegations when asked about the report, describing it as an "internal corporate matter", according to AFP.Technology analyst Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives described the investigation as a "black eye moment" for Huang. Ives said the controversy could trigger multiple congressional inquiries and create an overhang on Nvidia's stock.He also warned that the development could increase scrutiny of the company's chip sales to China, which remains a key issue in Washington.Huang's position at Nvidia could also come under scrutiny depending on the outcome of the board's investigation, Ives said, adding that the CEO's importance to the company's global strategy made the controversy a risk for the stock.Separately, Elon Musk responded to a social media post about the controversy. The post suggested that while Huang had done something incredibly foolish, there might have been no malicious intention. Musk replied, "I agree."Nvidia stock downNvidia shares came under pressure in out-of-hours trading following the announcement of the board investigation.Perpetual futures trading on the Hyperliquid exchange and after-hours shares trading on the Blue Ocean system showed Nvidia shares at around $180.30 on Monday, down approximately 3.4% from Friday's Nasdaq closing price of $186.64.The development has raised concerns about the potential impact of the controversy on investor sentiment, particularly given Huang's importance to Nvidia's business and its global AI strategy.South Korean govt intervenes in Nvidia CEO caseSouth Korea stated that Nvidia's contracted GPU deliveries to the country are expected to proceed without disruption despite the controversy surrounding Huang.Vice Science Minister Ryu Jemyung told a parliamentary budget committee on Monday that 10,000 GPUs funded under a 2025 supplementary budget had already arrived and were in use. GPUs planned for 2026 were under contract and expected to enter service this year."We expect production and the delivery schedule for contracted volumes to proceed without disruption," Ryu said, adding that the ministry was monitoring developments and discussing prices and schedules with Nvidia Korea.Meanwhile, a planned visit to South Korea by Huang's daughter Madison Huang, an Nvidia senior director, was cancelled.South Korean AI startup Rebellions said her planned visit to its headquarters and a dinner with partners had been called off due to unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia.Kakao Mobility also cancelled a photo session and question-and-answer event with her. However, the company said its business agreement with Nvidia would proceed, with senior director Gaurav Agarwal attending instead.Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to attract around 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, was proceeding as planned, according to South Korean media.The investigation's findings, the response from US lawmakers and any further developments concerning Megaspeed's business dealings with China will be key to determining the wider implications for Nvidia.

articles.title: Chandra and Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ
articles.summary: Mumbai: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday.Coming just days after the two were seen together at the wedding celebrations of Mehli's daughter Laila, the meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year marked by a broader power shift within the Tata Group following the death of Ratan Tata.Also read: Plea seeking Tata Sons listing filed in Bombay High CourtPeople familiar with the matter said Chandrasekaran and Mehli, who was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others, discussed issues that had affected their ties.Mehli-Chandra meet focused onrebuilding trust, restoring equationMehli's challenge against his removal is pending before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC).Mehli and Chandrasekaran's conversation last week was focused on rebuilding trust and restoring a working equation. Mehli later left for Dubai, with both sides appearing keen to move beyond a difficult period in one of Tata Group's most significant internal relationships.For much of the past decade, Mehli and Chandrasekaran were regarded as allies. After the dramatic ouster of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons in 2016, Mehli played a key role in the legal fight that followed between Cyrus and Ratan Tata. When Ratan Tata had to choose a successor, he picked Chandrasekaran, assisted by Mehli. Mehli later backed Chandrasekaran's second and third terms as chairman of Tata Sons. The third term, however, became contentious after Noel Tata, who succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's relationship survived differences in personality and style. Those who know Mehli describe him as intensely loyal, fiercely independent and refreshingly blunt. Friends admire his willingness to say in a room what others prefer to whisper outside it. Critics point to a temperament that can run ahead of diplomacy. The redeeming feature, according to people who have worked closely with him, is that his anger rarely lingers.Also read: Noel Tata proposes splitting Tata Sons as alternative to RBI-mandated listingChandrasekaran is a different kind of leader. Publicly measured and understated, he has cultivated the image of a consensus-builder since arriving at Bombay House. Yet colleagues say beneath that calm exterior lies a highly competitive executive with sharp political instincts and an acute understanding of institutional power.Then came the post-Ratan Tata era. Ratan Tata's death in Oct 2024 altered the balance of influence within Tata Trusts. Disagreements that had previously been settled privately soon surfaced within the trusts.Mehli and fellow Tata Trusts trustees Darius Khambata, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir Jehangir argued that information on Tata Sons covered under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association had not been shared with them, limiting their ability to take informed decisions. The four trustees voted Vijay Singh off the Tata Sons board.Concerns about the emerging situation prompted a visit to Delhi by Noel, Tata Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan, Khambata and Chandrasekaran, who briefed senior government officials on governance issues within the trusts.Mehli, who was inducted into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) by Ratan Tata and remained one of his most trusted advisers, increasingly found himself at odds with the emerging power structure. He was eventually voted out of the two trusts by Noel, Srinivasan and Singh, who is also a vice-chairman of the trusts.Among the relationships most affected was Mehli's equation with Chandrasekaran. Differences emerged over how developments within the trusts were characterised and communicated to external stakeholders, with Mehli maintaining that his interventions were driven by governance concerns. Communication between the two subsequently became infrequent.People said Chandrasekaran later made efforts, through intermediaries and directly, to reopen channels of communication with Mehli. Mehli remained a respected figure among trustees, a prominent voice within the Parsi community and an influential presence in discussions concerning the Tata legacy.Mehli has challenged the end of his trusteeship before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC), where the matter is pending. He, however, never withdrew his support for Chandrasekaran's stewardship of Tata Sons. In filings before the MCC, he said he had backed Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third five-year term and was a signatory to the resolution approving it.Chandrasekaran's second term as chairman ends in Feb 2027. His third term is linked to his continuation as a director of Tata Sons, which requires the trusts' approval at the company's annual general meeting (AGM). However, Tata Sons was unable to hold its AGM on Aug 18 after it failed to secure the requisite quorum. The impasse followed restrictions imposed by the MCC on SRTT, preventing it from joining SDTT in nominating a joint representative for quorum purposes.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina about to return to Bangladesh?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested on Monday a new passport and identity card so she can return from self-imposed exile in India, according to a letter seen by Reuters, her first such communication since fleeing in 2024.The request marks the clearest step by Hasina to act on her plan to return to Bangladesh in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising ended her long rule, raising the prospect of fresh political and legal tensions in a country where her party is now banned.Also read | G7 allies to assess impact of Trump's midterm setback at Paris talksShe has told Reuters she plans to return to surrender before a court, and her aides said on Monday the date would be announced once various formalities were completed. Bangladesh's war-crimes court sentenced her to death in November last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising, though she has denied the charges from exile."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers wrote to Preeti Rahman, acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi.The letter asked for the applications to be processed "expeditiously" on the basis of her Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".Rahman in Delhi and spokespeople for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in Dhaka did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Also read | Trump says his deportation policy 'might have been too tough' for votersHasina's Awami League party was the country's largest before it was banned following her fall. Many of her party colleagues have either been jailed or are in self-imposed exile in India or elsewhere.Having ruled Bangladesh for 20 years as prime minister across multiple terms, Hasina still enjoys support among sections of the population, and a return could sharpen political divisions as the government in Dhaka seeks to restore stability after more than two years of upheaval.On the other hand, it could improve Bangladesh's strained ties with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave her refuge.
